subject.title: [Bug] Telegram inbound images download but are not passed to model as vision input

question: Should current-turn image resolution forward successfully loaded native images when some same-turn image attachments fail, or should OpenClaw keep the current all-or-nothing fallback until a richer source-alignment contract exists?
rationale: The open closing PR changes shared channel message delivery semantics, and the safe implementation depends on the intended partial-media contract rather than a Telegram-only mechanical fix.

options.title: Repair aligned partial delivery
options.body: Allow partial native forwarding only after preserving original attachment positions through the prompt-image boundary, adding missing-first/missing-middle coverage, and collecting redacted Telegram or equivalent proof.

options.title: Keep all-or-nothing fallback
options.body: Preserve current fallback behavior and close or narrow the linked PR if partial native delivery is not the desired product contract.

options.title: Defer under canonical issue
options.body: Leave this issue open while maintainers settle the broader native-vision behavior and proof requirements for channel media.

recommendation.title: Repair aligned partial delivery
recommendation.body: Allow partial native forwarding only after preserving original attachment positions through the prompt-image boundary, adding missing-first/missing-middle coverage, and collecting redacted Telegram or equivalent proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc recently authored and merged the same resolver's mixed image-order contract and has the clearest recent ownership signal for the partial-media decision.
